question.text: The number of species below that have two lone pairs of electrons in their central atom is ___ (Round off to the Nearest integer) <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>SF</mi><mn>4</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>BF</mi><mn>4</mn><mo>-</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>ClF</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>AsF</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>PCl</mi><mn>5</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>BrF</mi><mn>5</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>XeF</mi><mn>4</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>SF</mi><mn>6</mn></msub></math>

solution.text:
Two l.p. on central atom is =ClF3,XeF4

The valence shell electron pair repulsion (VSEPR) theory is a model used to predict 3-D molecular geometry based on the number of valence shell electron bond pairs among the atoms in a molecule or ion. This model assumes that electron pairs will arrange themselves to minimize repulsion effects from one another.
